1: # 053 | Ordinary People: Autumn Transparent Watercolour
2: 
3: [Knowledge map](../README.md) · [Reading manual](../READING.md)
4: 
5: Reserved paper, transparent glazes, and an autumn setting carry a character's gaze and an unanswered relationship.
6: 
7: ## Editorial reading and design relationships
8: 
9: Paper white supplies light, wet handling describes sky and water, and local glazes develop foliage and figures. Warm leaves and a cool gray-blue environment serve the case's quiet sadness. These material differences explain more than the adjective soft alone.
10: 
11: The transferable relationship is between paper, transparent pigment, and local edge formation. Light areas can remain as paper; successive smaller glazes can deepen a form; a dried wash can leave a visible rim. These mechanisms can inform a bright interior or another palette. The autumn colors and quiet sadness explain this original choice rather than defining every watercolor proposal.
12: 
13: An empty lake, a son looking back at home, and his mother's lack of response form a chain of relationships. His lowered gaze and turn join the landscape in expressing mood. The complete context connects watercolor methods with the subject.
14: 
15: ## Further reading
16: 
17: - [Subject matter and visual language](../guides/theme.md): compare related designs within this topic.
18: - [How different media form an image](../guides/media.md): compare related designs within this topic.
19: - [From knowledge to a visual proposal](../guides/design-expression.md): Follow paper white and transparent glazing into a new bright-interior illustration proposal.
20: - [014 | How Green Was My Valley: Welsh Valley Gouache](../entries/opuscar-014.md): Compare how opaque gouache and transparent watercolor build landscape layers.
21: - [063 | Dances with Wolves: Field Journal · Pencil & Watercolour](../entries/opuscar-063.md): Compare emotional viewing with the context of field recording in watercolor.
22: 
23: ## Complete source material in English
24: 
25: The following is the preserved English original from OPUSCAR. Clawd, the orange identity color, and handoffs to neighboring films serve its anthology. Colors, actions, timings, and Avoid clauses belong to this case. The original project used code-based drawing and 3D rendering; these records do not establish per-case Bernini results. The complete bilingual record remains available at the source link below.
26: 
27: ![Original reference frame for Ordinary People](../../zyx/img/opuscar98/53.jpg)
28: 
29: ### Original identifiers and segment position
30: 
31: ```json
32: {
33:   "no": 53,
34:   "year": "1980",
35:   "title_en": "Ordinary People",
36:   "decade": "C6",
37:   "kind": "2D",
38:   "tone": "",
39:   "t0_seconds": 163.75,
40:   "duration_seconds": 2.5,
41:   "style_en": "Autumn Transparent Watercolour",
42:   "frame": "img/opuscar98/53.jpg"
43: }
44: ```
45: 
46: ### Ingredients
47: 
48: - Transparent watercolour glazes
49: - Winslow Homer and John Singer Sargent
50: - HB pencil underdrawing
51: 
52: ### Original author's design explanation
53: 
54: Transparent watercolour in layered glazes: wet-in-wet sky and lake, tide-mark edges, blooms, white paper left for highlights, autumn gold and rust against cool grey-blue. It matches the quiet, sad Lake Forest autumn of the film's opening.
55: 
56: ### Complete original style prompt
57: 
58: Transparent watercolour in layered glazes on cold-press paper. Draw shapes crisply first, then two or three glazes, each smaller and darker, drying to a tide-mark edge; two or three blooms, about 1/10 of frame width, inside large washes, never on figures; light granulation (±4%). Paper is the brightest white; light objects and highlights left as paper. Sky and water wet-in-wet, ripples dry-brush. Roles: autumn gold #ECAA34, scarlet #E46030, rust #B8743C for foliage and accents, against grey-blue mist #C2C6D2 and violet-grey shadows #8A8496; sky pale and cool at any time of day; ground pale green-ochre. Foliage: pale wash, scallop-edged clusters, dark dots, flicked leaves; with few trees, warm colours go to scrub, roofs, clothes. Light from one side. Camera: slow pan, gentle push, leaves drifting past the lens. Reference: Winslow Homer's watercolours. Avoid: opaque gouache, airbrushed blur, vector edges, muddy colour, saturated sunsets.
59: 
60: ### All shots in their original order
61: 
62: #### 1. lake | 0.8 seconds
63: 
64: Empty dawn shot of Lake Michigan: a paper-white sun path on grey-blue water, then a slow pan right to the autumn bluff.
65: 
66: #### 2. still | 1.0 seconds
67: 
68: The street under the maples: Clawd as Conrad, long striped scarf and satchel, stops on the sidewalk and turns to look back at the white colonial house where Calvin rakes leaves, then drops its eyes and turns away; a slow drift right with a slight pull back.
69: 
70: #### 3. porch | 0.7 seconds
71: 
72: Beth on the porch, arms folded, cold; the camera creeps in on her.
73: 
74: ### Direction and handoff
75: 
76: Clawd plays Conrad: a long navy-and-cream school scarf blown by the lake wind, and a leather satchel. The scene runs at 1.1× throughout, as slow as the Pachelbel opening. Three hard cuts: the lake, the son looking back at the house, the mother who gives nothing back. Its eyes moving from the house to the ground is the whole performance.
77: 
78: ### References named by the author
79: 
80: Robert Redford, Ordinary People (1980) · John Bailey (cinematography) · Winslow Homer (watercolours) · John Singer Sargent (watercolours)
81: 
82: The named artists, filmmakers, and works are the original author's reference statements; they were not individually verified through external historical research in this reorganization.
83:

85:

Read those fragments with the complete design above. Default risk fields such as `identity_risk`, and `common_failure_modes` derived from Avoid clauses, are converter annotations or author advice rather than measured failure records.

1: # 063 | Dances with Wolves: Field Journal · Pencil & Watercolour
2: 
3: [Knowledge map](../README.md) · [Reading manual](../READING.md)
4: 
5: Drawing a journal becomes a route into the prairie, where a relationship with a wolf develops through the recorder's viewpoint.
6: 
7: ## Editorial reading and design relationships
8: 
9: Pencil visible through watercolor, handwritten arrows, and paper traces establish field recording. Color is applied from far to near, making the viewer aware of both the represented scene and its formation as a record.
10: 
11: Visible pencil and transparent color share the work of describing the scene: pressure-varied lines articulate forms, while washes add color without fully covering them. This relationship can support a new illustration with its own subject and palette. The labels, yellowed journal, sunset, and opening color-arrival sequence each add another function and can be considered separately.
12: 
13: The camera approaches as color appears, then enters a full-frame prairie where the figure tips his hat to the wolf. Recording support, image formation, and event remain connected. Cases retaining visible pages or collage frames offer further comparisons.
14: 
15: ## Further reading
16: 
17: - [Combining styles and methods](../guides/combination.md): compare related designs within this topic.
18: - [Video meaning and design possibilities](../guides/meaning.md): compare related designs within this topic.
19: - [From knowledge to a visual proposal](../guides/design-expression.md): Follow visible pencil and transparent color into a new storybook proposal, with journal and sunset choices kept in their source context.
20: - [069 | The English Patient: Explorer's Scrapbook Watercolour](../entries/opuscar-069.md): Compare entering a scene through a single journal page and a collage of materials.
21: - [053 | Ordinary People: Autumn Transparent Watercolour](../entries/opuscar-053.md): Compare similar watercolor methods in field recording and an emotional landscape.
22: 
23: ## Complete source material in English
24: 
25: The following is the preserved English original from OPUSCAR. Clawd, the orange identity color, and handoffs to neighboring films serve its anthology. Colors, actions, timings, and Avoid clauses belong to this case. The original project used code-based drawing and 3D rendering; these records do not establish per-case Bernini results. The complete bilingual record remains available at the source link below.
26:

28: 
29: ### Original identifiers and segment position
30:

33:   "no": 63,
34:   "year": "1990",
35:   "title_en": "Dances with Wolves",
36:   "decade": "C7",
37:   "kind": "2D",
38:   "tone": "",

40:   "duration_seconds": 2.5,
41:   "style_en": "Field Journal · Pencil & Watercolour",
42:   "frame": "img/opuscar98/63.jpg"
43: }
44: ```
45: 
46: ### Ingredients
47: 
48: - Graphite under-drawing
49: - Transparent watercolour
50: - Iron-gall ink handwriting
51: - Bodmer and Catlin field sketches
52: 
53: ### Original author's design explanation
54: 
55: A soldier's field journal: pressure-varied pencil, transparent watercolour, yellowed rag paper, inked script and pencil notes in the margins. Dunbar writes and sketches in his diary throughout the film, so the prairie appears as his sketch coming to life.
56: 
57: ### Complete original style prompt
58: 
59: A 19th-century field journal come to life: full-colour watercolour over visible pencil. Pencil under-drawing #3A363A, pressure-varied and broken, lightly hatched in shadow, readable through the washes. Brushed washes with soft wet edges, blooms, pooled rims and granulation (not flat polygons) cover about 80% of the frame in rich warm colour. Default magic hour: dusty-rose sky #C88F76 turning lavender above, streaky rose clouds, low sun, ochre-gold land #DEBE87, violet distance, long shadows, opaque pale-gold lifts on sun-facing edges. Yellowed rag paper #F0E4C8, faint stains and foxing, showing through. Iron-gall ink #34221C for small labels and arrows. Signature move, once at the opening (about 2 s): bare pencil, then colour arrives wash by wash, far to near, during a push-in; after that, full colour. References: Bodmer and Catlin field sketches. Avoid: grey, muddy or pale washes; uniform digital outlines; later pencil-only frames.
60: 
61: ### All shots in their original order
62: 
63: #### 1. page | 1.2 seconds
64: 
65: Push in on the journal's right page: Clawd's self-portrait and the wolf Two Socks start as bare pencil and are coloured in stroke by stroke, sky first, Clawd last.
66: 
67: #### 2. prairie | 1.3 seconds
68: 
69: Cut to the sketch come alive in full colour at sunset: one push from the plain in to Clawd and Two Socks facing each other, the buffalo herd running behind; Clawd tips its hat.
70: 
71: ### Direction and handoff
72: 
73: Clawd plays Dunbar: a black cavalry officer's hat with gold cord, the journal in one hand and a pencil in the other. The push and the colouring-in are one gesture; the cut to the living prairie comes mid-phrase, and the hat tip lands on the last beats. 1:1 time.
74: 
75: ### References named by the author
76: 
77: Kevin Costner, Dances with Wolves (1990) · Dean Semler (cinematography) · Dances with Wolves (1990) poster · Karl Bodmer · George Catlin
78:

materials.text:
1: # Bernini-R: concrete style expression in the October 29 probe
2: 
3: [Knowledge map](../README.md) · [Experience synthesis](../guides/experience.md) · [From knowledge to a proposal](../guides/design-expression.md) · [Reading manual](../READING.md)
4: 
5: Evidence status: synthesis of an existing exploratory run and its recorded reviews. This page adds no new generation or model evaluation. Its current operational use concerns style expression; semantic-preservation strategies are deferred.
6: 
7: ## Run conditions
8: 
9: The probe used the official Bernini renderer with direct prompts and no legacy Planner. There were four source clips and ten conditions, one independent generation per condition with seed 42. The model was `ByteDance/Bernini-R-1.3B-Diffusers`, revision `ff4c5d4d2d31365c2ffeb30e9753065ee18f58ce`: 40 inference steps, `v2v_apg`, maximum image size 848, empty negative prompt, and prompt enhancer disabled.
10: 
11: Eight main-set deliveries are five seconds, 100 frames at 20 fps. The two table-tennis deliveries are approximately 4.43 seconds, 133 frames at 30 fps. Native versus delivered frame counts and source-frame mapping are documented in the result records and [frame-mapping audit](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/frame-mapping-audit.json). Per-condition `input.json` retains the prompt, system prefix, effective text, and token count. These records distinguish authored text from the actual text prepared for the model.
12: 
13: The primary reviews used GPT-6.1-sol with xhigh reasoning on 12 sampled frames per clip. The 041 paired review used six sampled frames per clip. [Evaluation provenance](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/evaluation-provenance.json) records the execution hosts and review scope. Sampling supports appearance judgments and broad comparisons; exact continuous motion requires different evidence.
14: 
15: ## What the existing results contribute
16: 
17: | Task and conditions | Recorded appearance | Implication for knowledge use |
18: |---|---|---|
19: | main/027: short, long, long_keep | The short etching label produced a recognizable etched image and added celestial/cloud forms. Detailed descriptions more closely specified black contours, hatching, ivory paper, and an open sky. | A label can activate a medium. Knowledge can refine its visible character and distribution across the image. |
20: | main/041: short, long, long_keep | The short storybook request remained largely photographic. Both detailed versions produced clear watercolor-and-pencil illustration. | Developing one interpretation into visible marks, colors, shadow treatment, and support texture is a useful direction for this model and task. |
21: | fewshot/004: long, long_keep | Both versions produced a space-station environment, Earth view, and technical clothing. Blue glow appeared mainly on the lower table supports. | Overall setting and clothing can work while a local effect lands on a different part. Name the intended part clearly when developing the proposal; a wording fix remains untested. |
22: | main/024: long, long_keep | Both versions produced substantial glitch treatment. The additional-clause version was judged to have more complete RGB separation. | The prompt's described effects provide an inspectable visual direction. This comparison offers no isolated test of effect vocabulary or clause order. |
23: 
24: The synthesis draws on the individual judgments, the existing [comparison page](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/comparison.html), and [review notes](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/review_notes.json). The latter two are original historical artifacts in their original language; this English working record supplies navigation and a scoped interpretation.
25: 
26: The useful finding is that concrete visual elaboration helped express the chosen styles in these runs. Longer prompts also contained more information, so the experiment leaves their separate contributions unresolved. Storybook watercolor is one interpretation of a broad label; the short request did not itself demand its pastel palette. The 027 result shows that short labels can also work.
27: 
28: ## Guidance available to a Planner
29: 
30: Use medium and design knowledge to develop a coherent visible interpretation. Describe relevant relationships: pencil visible through a transparent wash, hatching building darker foliage, light emitted by a particular surface, or RGB separation affecting a specified image region. Select details because they contribute to the current design. The [application guide](../guides/design-expression.md) demonstrates this with complete-source reading paths.
31: 
32: The experiment motivates explicit object, part, and region wording as a clarity measure. Its table-tennis results also show why a well-specified intention and an achieved placement need separate records. The new tabletop-rim sentence in the application guide is a candidate for later testing, with its untested status kept alongside it.
33: 
34: Prompt order, optimum length, compulsory opening scene descriptions, fixed word counts, and a universal style vocabulary were not isolated in this probe. This record provides conditional guidance that a later expression interface can consult; it supplies no mandatory prompt template. Source materials and user requests continue to determine the design content.
35: 
36: ## Boundaries of this evidence
37: 
38: The ten conditions were independent single outputs, with no repeated seeds or multi-round refinement. The results concern this Bernini model revision and setup. The separate Ditto smoke test provides no corresponding style-quality conclusion.
39: 
40: The `long_keep` inputs and their reviews remain available below for accurate provenance. The table-tennis `long` input already contains preservation wording. Their comparison is therefore an addition of further clauses. Semantic outcomes remain in the original records; this revision does not derive a preservation recipe from them. The [041 paired review](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/041-paired-review.json) supersedes the earlier apparent object-preservation advantage: both illustrated variants simplified the implement and weakened the notebook's construction.
41: 
42: ## Evidence chain and complete inputs
43: 
44: [Case definitions and settings](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/cases.json) · [Preflight](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/preflight.json) · [Run summary](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/run-summary.json) · [Local output verification](../../out/prompt_probe/20261029_bernini/local-output-verification.json) · [Renderer script](../../scripts/deploy/run_prompt_probe.py) · [Review script](../../scripts/deploy/judge_prompt_probe.py)
45:

Each input record provides the effective text; each result record provides delivered duration and output hash; each judgment supplies the recorded interpretation. Prompts are historical experimental inputs, including any imperative clauses they contain.
